extraction_notes:
SCOPE. Three lanes: (A) preclinical in-vivo platelet data with animal-to-human translation, (B) non-ASO
modalities and well-sourced negative controls, (C) megakaryocyte / bone-marrow production axis.
Nothing on the do-not-re-extract list was used. All 19 oligos and 50 measurements below come from
documents actually fetched and read in this session (26 rows graded 0, 11 graded 1, 4 graded 2, 9 graded 3).

WHAT WAS FETCHED AND PARSED
- 14 FDA review PDFs downloaded from accessdata.fda.gov with a browser User-Agent (the .cfm table-of-contents
  pages all return 404 now; only direct PDF URLs work, so filenames were brute-forced across the
  {PharmR, MedR, MultidisciplineR, MultiR, OtherR, SumR, ClinPharmR, ChemR, Approv, RiskR, StatR} x year grid).
  Text extracted with PyMuPDF and grepped for platelet|thrombocyt|megakaryo.
  Hits: mipomersen 44 (not used - covered elsewhere), patisiran 17, olezarsen 12, nusinersen 1,
  inclisiran-MedR 8, vutrisiran-MedR 6, givosiran 5, eteplirsen 5, casimersen 1.
  Zero hits (logged as negatives, no rows): golodirsen PharmR, viltolarsen PharmR, inclisiran PharmR,
  vutrisiran PharmR, tofersen OtherR, eplontersen OtherR, donidalorsen OtherR, fitusiran OtherR,
  lumasiran OtherR, nedosiran OtherR.
- 7 EMA EPAR assessment reports (Givlaari, Oxlumo, Leqvio, Amvuttra, Onpattro, Spinraza, Qalsody).
  Platelet content in Amvuttra, Oxlumo, Onpattro, Spinraza, Qalsody; none in Leqvio or Givlaari.
- 12 DailyMed SPLs for section-11 design metadata.
- Europe PMC / PubMed for the literature arm.

LANE A - PRECLINICAL IN VIVO (36 animal_invivo rows: 22 monkey, 8 rat, 6 mouse; 14 clinical rows sit in Lane B)
Monkey is where the ASO signal lives, and the three Ionis monkey papers are the backbone:
Henry 2017 (class database, 102 ASOs / 61 studies / >2200 NHPs), Narayanan 2018 (ISIS 104838 mechanism,
111In platelet kinetics) and Shen 2023 (ISIS 405879, complement, monkey colony source). All three are
PAYWALLED - academic.oup.com and the Liebert/SAGE host both returned HTTP 403 - so values come from the
PubMed abstracts, which do carry quantitative results. Those rows are therefore cited to 'Abstract (Results)'
rather than to a numbered table, and are classed summary_stat. This is the one place where I could not
name a table locus; I judged the abstracts to be a defensible locus because they state the numbers
themselves, but a reviewer may prefer to demote them.

ANIMAL-TO-HUMAN TRANSLATION was captured explicitly, as requested:
1. Henry 2017 (row: ISIS 404173, human, Phase 2): the consistent self-limiting group-mean decline seen in
   NHP DOES appear to translate to humans but is of limited clinical significance, whereas
   'NHPs appear to OVERPREDICT the incidence of sporadic PLT <50K cells/uL compared to humans.'
   Concretely: 1/16 NHP at 10 mg/kg/wk and 3/16 at 20 mg/kg/wk fell below 50 x10^9/L, while 62 patients
   at 200 mg/wk (~3.3 mg/kg/wk) for 26 weeks produced no value below 75 x10^9/L. Exposures are not matched,
   which is itself part of why the monkey over-predicts.
2. Shen 2023: the monkey's predictive value is COLONY-DEPENDENT - 7/9 Mauritian-sourced vs 0 Asian-sourced
   cynomolgus monkeys developed <50 x10^9/L on the same ASO at the same dose. Any 'monkey incidence' quoted
   for this endpoint is meaningless without the animal source.
3. The FDA immunology assessor in the olezarsen review (NDA 218614 OtherR) states the complement arm of the
   monkey mechanism 'is not evident in humans' - i.e. a monkey-specific amplifier. Logged in sources_found.
4. Narayanan 2018 vs the human inotersen story: the monkey mechanism is antibody/complement-mediated
   peripheral clearance (hepatic/splenic sequestration +60-80%, anti-PF4 and anti-platelet IgM), with
   monocyte but NOT platelet activation - the same axis as the human anti-GPIIb/IIIa IgG cases,
   which is why the monkey gets the mechanism right even while over-predicting the incidence.

A cross-modality nuance worth flagging for the PS hypothesis: in the patisiran rat programme the LNP-packaged
anti-luciferase control AF-011-1955 produced a statistically significant platelet fall (-28% in males)
at a dose where the patisiran siRNA itself did not, i.e. part of the rodent LNP platelet effect is
vehicle-driven, not oligonucleotide-driven.

LANE B - NEGATIVE CONTROLS (26 grade-0 rows out of 50 total)
Every grade-0 row is a REPORTED no-effect, never silence. Discipline applied:
- GRADE 0 ACCEPTED where a document states that platelets were measured and unchanged, or prints an
  explicit zero: inclisiran Table 88 (Platelets <=75 x10^9/L: 0.0% vs 0.0% in ORION-9; 0/811 vs 1/804
  placebo in ORION-11, i.e. the only event was on placebo); vutrisiran and patisiran in FDA Table 24
  (an FDA-generated shift table); patisiran APOLLO (no patient <50 x10^9/L, and the mean nadir excursion
  was SMALLER on drug, -11, than on placebo, -23); vutrisiran and patisiran EMA EPARs; tofersen EMA EPAR
  ('no difference in platelet counts over time between the placebo and tofersen-treated participants');
  eteplirsen 39-week monkey and safety-pharmacology monkey studies, where platelet count is itemised in
  the analysed panel and other haematology changes ARE reported but platelets are not among them;
  givosiran 39-week monkey ('Hematology: Unremarkable at the end of dosing'); lumasiran monkey studies,
  where PLT is in the table legend and platelet changes are reported for the rat rows of the same table.
- GRADE 0 REFUSED for revusiran, despite having its full CC-BY nonclinical safety paper: it never mentions
  platelets. Also refused for the 10 FDA reviews with zero platelet hits, and for every approved-oligo label
  whose text never mentions platelets. These are logged as negatives in sources_found instead.
- ADJACENT-HAEMATOLOGY FALLBACK (is_platelet_specific=FALSE, 6 rows) used where a review says 'standard
  battery of hematology parameters ... no test article-related effects' without itemising platelets:
  golodirsen (monkey, mouse), viltolarsen (monkey), casimersen (monkey, mouse), nusinersen (EMA clinical).

Result for the hypothesis (PS content + protein binding drive platelet effects): it holds, with two
qualifications the data force. The four neutral-backbone PMOs are grade 0 up to 320-640 mg/kg/week in
39-week monkey studies - roughly 60-100x the weekly mg/kg of the ASO doses that cause severe monkey
thrombocytopenia. The GalNAc-siRNAs are grade 0 in monkey (givosiran to 100 mg/kg/wk, lumasiran to
300 mg/kg/month) and in ~1833 inclisiran-treated humans. But (i) a PMO CAN lower platelets 23% in mdx
mice at 960 mg/kg/wk IV, so a neutral backbone is not absolutely protective at extreme exposure, and
(ii) tofersen carries 15 phosphorothioate linkages of 19 yet shows no human platelet signal when given
INTRATHECALLY - route/systemic exposure, not PS count alone, is the operative variable.

LANE C - MEGAKARYOCYTE / BONE MARROW: ESSENTIALLY EMPTY, REPORTED HONESTLY
Four Europe PMC searches ('phosphorothioate oligonucleotide megakaryocyte'; 'oligonucleotide bone marrow
megakaryocyte toxicity monkey'; 'megakaryocyte antisense oligonucleotide in vitro proplatelet CD34';
'MEG-01 OR Dami megakaryocytic cell line oligonucleotide phosphorothioate'; 'iPSC derived megakaryocytes
oligonucleotide safety assay platelet production'; 'antisense oligonucleotide bone marrow megakaryocyte
hyperplasia rat mouse histopathology') returned NO paper in which an oligonucleotide is applied to
CD34+-derived, MEG-01/Dami/K562 or iPSC-derived megakaryocytes with megakaryocyte number, ploidy,
proplatelet formation or viability as the readout. Hits were dominated by unrelated haematology and by
conference abstract books. Likewise, none of the 14 FDA reviews or 7 EPARs parsed here reports a
bone-marrow megakaryocyte histopathology finding for any of these compounds. ZERO megakaryocyte rows are
therefore submitted. This is a genuine gap in the public literature, not a search failure I can close.
What the retrieved sources DO say about the production axis is indirect and consistent: Narayanan 2018
localises platelet loss to hepatic/splenic sequestration (destruction, not production), and the companion
human study (PMID 32043907, abstract) states that direct myelotoxicity was ruled out in inotersen patients.
The CC-BY NAT 2023 preclinical-assessment review (PMC9940817) lists only peripheral platelet-activation
assays (CD62P, PAC-1 in PRP/whole blood) for the thrombocytopenia endpoint - it proposes no megakaryocyte
assay at all, which is itself evidence that no validated megakaryocyte model for this endpoint exists.

WHAT FAILED
- Full texts of Henry 2017, Narayanan 2018, Shen 2023, Johansson 2024: HTTP 403 / paywalled. Abstracts used.
- Pegaptanib (Macugen, NDA 21-756) FDA pharmacology review: downloads fine but is an image-only scan with
  no text layer (1,944 extractable bytes across 114 pages). No aptamer rows. OCR would be needed.
  With pegaptanib unreadable and no platelet data found for pegnivacogin/REG1, the APTAMER class is
  UNCOVERED in this lane - flagged as the main remaining gap alongside Lane C.
- Fitusiran, nedosiran, eplontersen, donidalorsen: reviews and labels retrieved, no platelet content, no rows.
- Revusiran: full CC-BY nonclinical paper retrieved, no platelet content, no rows (see above).
- accessdata.fda.gov TOC .cfm pages return 404 for every application tried, so review filenames had to be
  guessed; some applications (lumasiran, nedosiran, fitusiran) appear to have no posted PharmR/MultidisciplineR
  at all, only ChemR/OtherR/RiskR/Approv, which limits what could be checked for them.

PROVENANCE
Every row carries source_id + source_ref + source_table. Regulatory documents are public_domain;
the four paywalled journal sources are summary_stat; the two CC-BY articles are labelled cc_by with the
licence read from the article's own licence field (both verified: PMC9940817 'Creative Commons License
[CC-BY]', PMC6987735 same) - though neither ultimately yielded a measurement row.
No sequence and no toxicity value in this file was recalled from memory; where a value was not visible in
fetched text it is TBD. ps_count is given only where the label states it (inclisiran 6, tofersen 15) or where
the label's molecular formula contains no sulfur at all (patisiran 0); for the GalNAc-siRNAs whose formulas
show S6 I left ps_count TBD and recorded the formula in the oligo notes rather than deriving the count.

measurements.notes: ANIMAL-TO-HUMAN TRANSLATION (the key row of this lane). Authors' conclusion, verbatim: 'the consistent, self-limiting PLT reduction seen in NHP may translate to humans, but these changes appear to be of limited clinical significance. However, NHPs appear to OVERPREDICT the incidence of sporadic PLT <50K cells/uL compared to humans.' So: monkey group-mean decline -> translates (grade 1 in both); monkey sporadic severe thrombocytopenia -> OVER-predicts human risk. Human exposure ~3.3 mg/kg/wk vs 10-20 mg/kg/wk in the NHP study, so the comparison is not exposure-matched.

measurements.notes: Mauritian-sourced cynomolgus monkeys are markedly MORE susceptible to 2'-MOE-ASO-induced thrombocytopenia than Asian-sourced animals. This is a major confounder for animal-to-human translation: the apparent incidence of severe ASO thrombocytopenia in monkey depends on the colony source, so a monkey study's predicted human risk is source-dependent.

measurements.notes: Graded 2 (moderate) rather than 3 because the abstract does not give a platelet count or a severity band - only 'acute dose-dependent thrombocytopenia'. Mechanism: TLR9- and Syk-dependent, IVIg-rescuable, with raised plasma MCP-1; CpG ODN also activated human platelets in vitro and drove Syk-dependent phagocytosis by THP-1 monocytes. IMPORTANT INTERNAL NEGATIVE CONTROL in the same experiment: mice treated with a 2'-O-methoxyethyl-modified antisense ODN did NOT become thrombocytopenic, i.e. the acute murine effect is CpG/TLR9-driven and sequence-motif-dependent, not a generic oligonucleotide effect. That comparator ASO is unnamed in the abstract, so no separate row is created for it.

sources_found.data_description: No new numeric platelet data, but an FDA immunology assessor's mechanistic statement of record: PS-ASOs bind platelet GPVI (causing aggregation) and PF4 (a HIT-like humoral response), and 'marked increases in platelet-bound C3d/C4d were observed in 2'-MOE ASO-induced thrombocytopenic monkeys, indicating increased platelet clearance due to complement deposition ... While this complement activation is not evident in humans, the non-clinical data certainly raises concerns.' A regulator-authored animal-to-human translation statement. 0 measurement rows taken (no values, and olezarsen is covered by another lane).

Rabbit is not in the species controlled vocabulary, so no row was created.
